HELD 2026-09-19, and THE PREVIOUS HOLD REASON WAS WRONG -- the third such note in one day. It said the edition breaks no paragraph before a speaker, so speeches land in the wrong mouth mid-line. It does break one, every time: every speaker opens a

, a block boundary, or a page break. The five merges were the pipeline falling back to heuristic plain-text parsing because NO rule matched this edition, not the edition failing to mark. Measured: the page marks 65 speeches across 14 characters in 3.1; V.mark_speakers claims 0 and the heuristic tail returns 56. The vocabulary is known and written up in docs/2026-09-19-shakespeare-vendoring/chinese_edition_diagnosis.md -- speaker is 1-4 CJK chars + U+3000 at a paragraph head, block business is a centred div opening with a fullwidth black bracket, headings match ^第.*[幕场場]$ and must be exempted or the scene anchors break. THE TRAP, corroborated independently by two sources: _marked_name rejects len(name) < 2, and most of this cast is ONE character (波, 衮, 蒂, 勃, 弗) -- the rule can mark every speaker correctly and still drop them all downstream. Needs a per-edition rule, not a mid-line pre-pass.
